<p> NIGERIA’s Super Eagles have been weakened by club restrictions and injuries ahead of Tuesday’s international friendly against Russia’s senior men’s national team.</p>



<p>The <a href="https://nannews.ng/">News Agency of Nigeria (NAN)</a> reports that Captain Wilfred Ndidi was ruled out after sustaining a minor knock during last week’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifier against Guinea-Bissau.</p>



<p>Midfielder Raphael Onyedika was also prevented from travelling to Russia after his German club, Eintracht Frankfurt, declined to release him for the friendly.</p>



<p>Defender Bright Osayi-Samuel and UAE-based midfielder Ridwan Abdulrasaq Popoola were similarly stopped by their clubs from joining the squad.</p>



<p>Switzerland-based defender Victory Akpe also missed the trip after sustaining an injury, further reducing the options available to Head Coach Éric Chelle.</p>



<p>Austria-based Moses Usor, who scored on his Nigeria debut against Madagascar in Uyo on Sept. 25, was initially not listed for the trip.</p>



<p>However, after Chelle requested his release, LASK FC instructed the player not to travel to Russia for the friendly.</p>



<p>Suleiman Mubarak, invited from Slavia Prague of Czechia, was also unable to travel because his residence permit had not been secured.</p>



<p>The setbacks have left Nigeria with a depleted squad for the encounter against Russia, who held the Super Eagles to a 1-1 draw in Moscow 16 months ago.</p>



<p>The late invitee, Ibraheem Ajasa of FC Rostov, was expected to join the team’s camp in Nizhny Novgorod on Sunday evening.</p>



<p>18 SUPER EAGLES IN RUSSIA FOR FRIENDLY</p>



<p>Goalkeepers: Michael Atata (Ikorodu City); Samuel James (SJK FC, Finland); Stanley Nwabali (Chippa United, South Africa).</p>



<p>Defenders: Kenneth Igboke (Enugu Rangers); Isaac James (Alverca FC, Portugal); Benjamin Fredricks (Brentford FC, England); Emmanuel Fernandez (Glasgow Rangers, Scotland); Abdullahi Bewene (FC Banik Ostrava, Czechia).</p>



<p>Midfielders: Chibuzo Nwoke (Fulham FC, England); Stephen Michael (Vendsyssel FF, Denmark); Igor Wilfred (Kristiansund FC, Norway); Aderemi Adeoye (Ikorodu City).</p>



<p>Forwards: Kelechi Iheanacho (Bursaspor FC, Turkey); Moses Simon (Paris FC, France); Akor Adams (Venezia FC, Italy); Peter Edokpolor (SL Benfica, Portugal); Abubakar Umar (FC Famalicao, Portugal); Abdullahi Umar (Hradec Kralove, Czechia).(<a href="https://nannews.ng/">NAN</a>)</p>

				const lazyloadRunObserver = () => {
					const lazyloadBackgrounds = document.querySelectorAll( `.e-con.e-parent:not(.e-lazyloaded)` );
					const lazyloadBackgroundObserver = new IntersectionObserver( ( entries ) => {
						entries.forEach( ( entry ) => {
							if ( entry.isIntersecting ) {
								let lazyloadBackground = entry.target;
								if( lazyloadBackground ) {
									lazyloadBackground.classList.add( 'e-lazyloaded' );

								lazyloadBackgroundObserver.unobserve( entry.target );

					lazyloadBackgrounds.forEach( ( lazyloadBackground ) => {
						lazyloadBackgroundObserver.observe( lazyloadBackground );

				};
				const events = [
					'DOMContentLoaded',

				];
